web_blocks.html: Executive Thesis: Texas Instruments (NASDAQ: TXN) is exiting a four-year capital cycle with a wider moat. From 2023 to 2025, TI spent $14.44B on 300mm fabs (RFAB2, LFAB1/2, SM1/SM2) during an industry downturn.[1][4] In 2026, cash flow turned sharply higher. Q3 2026 sales jumped 28% YoY to $6.06B, while gross margin rose 720 bps from FY2025 to 64.2%.[2] Capex also fell toward the $2B–$3B target ($2.58B TTM). TTM free cash flow hit $8.42B ($6.82B ex-CHIPS grants), easily covering the ~$5.2B dividend.[2] TI earns a clear COMPOUNDER_PASS on quality. We flag PASS_WITH_WATCH on 194-day inventory and the $7.5B Silicon Labs deal closing in H1 2027.[2][6]

Why WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT ($278.00–$286.00) Instead of Buying at $303.60: At $303.60 (26.06x Forward P/E, 26.19x EV/EBITDA, 1.90% yield), TXN already prices in a smooth 2027 FCF ramp.[12][13] The stock is up +86.80% over the past year. Meanwhile, the US market sits in a Correction with 6 distribution days in 25 sessions (SPY $754.37, QQQ $679.89).[15] Buying at $303.60 gives just 1.00:1 reward-to-risk to our $345.00 Base target (+13.6%) versus our $262.00 stop (-13.7%). Waiting for the $278.00–$286.00 support shelf lifts asymmetry to 2.46:1.[13] That zone aligns S1 ($277.54), 50D SMA ($283.87), 10W EMA ($285.85), and 30W SMA ($286.10). Existing Schwab shares (1.6917 shares, $499.98 basis, 0.58% weight) stay HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP at $262.00.[17]

Three-Horizon & Capital-Allocation Summary: Over 1 to 12 weeks, we rate new capital WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT so we avoid buying into a weak tape. Over 3 to 18 months, higher 300mm fab output and the H1 2027 Silicon Labs close drive strong earnings growth. Over 3 to 10 years, TXN remains a top CORE_ALPHA (TIER_2) compounder. It boasts 22.04% ROIC, 23 straight years of dividend hikes ($6.08 annualized), and >95% internal wafers by 2030.[4][9][12]

Key Risks & Falsification Triggers: Three risks could hurt this thesis. First, a deeper industrial or auto slump could idle 300mm fabs and push inventory past 210 days. Second, Chinese analog rivals (SG Micro, 3PEAK, Silergy) and tariffs could cut TI's ~19%–20% China sales.[2][8] Third, the $7.5B all-cash Silicon Labs deal could face integration delays or debt strain.[6] A daily or weekly close below $262.00 triggers an immediate exit of our 1.6917 Schwab shares.[13][17]

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our institutional underwriting dossier on Texas Instruments Incorporated. Before we dive into ten chapters of history, factory economics, competitive warfare, and valuation math, let us put the entire investment thesis on one clear page.

On the business itself, Texas Instruments earns an unambiguous COMPOUNDER_PASS. Over the past four years, management did something rare in public markets: it spent $14.44 billion building 300-millimeter wafer fabs in Texas and Utah right through a two-year industrial and automotive downturn. In 2026, that contrarian bet turned into an unmistakable cash-flow inflection. Third-quarter 2026 revenue jumped 28% year-over-year to $6.06 billion, gross margin rebounded 720 basis points to 64.2%, capital spending stepped down into the $2 billion to $3 billion framework, and trailing twelve-month free cash flow surged to $8.42 billion—or $6.82 billion even after stripping out $1.6 billion in CHIPS Act incentives.

Yet great businesses do not automatically make great immediate entries at every price. At $303.60 per share on November 13, 2026, TXN trades at 26.06 times forward earnings after an 86.80% rally over the past twelve months, while the broader US equity market sits in a six-distribution-day Correction. Buying at $303.60 leaves a flat 1.00-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio between our $345.00 base target and our $262.00 structural stop-loss.

Therefore, our dual verdict is disciplined and crystal clear. For new capital, the verdict is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT in the $278.00 to $286.00 institutional shelf—where the S1 pivot, 50-day SMA, 10-week EMA, and 30-week SMA converge to lift reward-to-risk to 2.46-to-1. For our existing Schwab position of 1.6917 shares ($499.98 cost basis, 0.58% weight), the action is HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP at $262.00, selling zero shares and keeping 100% of sidelined cash ready for support.

book_subsections.title: What to Watch Across the Next Four Quarters
paragraphs: Three operational signposts will determine whether TXN marches toward our $390.00 bull case or slips toward our $225.00 bear case: first, Days of Inventory continuing down from 194 days toward 150–170 days without gross margin dipping below 60%; second, smooth H1 2027 closing and 300mm fab migration of the $7.5 billion Silicon Labs acquisition; and third, defending Western industrial, automotive, and data-center power sockets while Chinese fabless rivals pressure commodity analog inside mainland China.

In the pages ahead, Chapters 1 through 6 walk you through the entire business on a strictly price-blind basis—from TXN's 1930 oil-seismograph origins and 1997–2012 portfolio pruning, to its 80,000-product catalog, 300mm wafer unit economics, China competitive dynamics, Haviv Ilan's KPI scorecard, and ten-year cash-flow forensics. Chapters 7 through 9 then bring in the November 13, 2026 market tape: the $303.60 Reverse DCF, six-peer valuation matrix, Weinstein Stage 2 chart, cheap Sept 2027 LEAPS Call, and our probability-weighted action plan.

Keep in mind the central lesson of this dossier: separating business quality from entry price is the single highest-value habit in institutional investing. Texas Instruments is a world-class analog franchise exiting peak capital intensity, yet even a world-class franchise can deliver mediocre 12-month returns if bought extended in a correcting market. By holding our 1.6917 Schwab shares with a $262.00 structural stop and keeping 100% of new capital in cash until TXN tests the $278.00–$286.00 shelf, we respect both the business moat and the tape.

Finally, note how the options market complements our equity patience. Because TXN's at-the-money implied volatility (49.6%) sits below 20-day realized volatility (57.1%), our Options Desk identifies an IV-cheap LONG_CALL_LEAPS setup—the September 17, 2027 $280 Call near $64.53 per share ($6,453.00 maximum possible loss, 0.69 delta, -$9.81/day theta). Crucially, this 2027-09-17 $280 LEAPS Call is gated strictly on a pullback to the $278.00–$286.00 support shelf, consistent with WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT—never an immediate entry at $303.60 into six market distribution days.

In addition, our 100%-reconciled capital redeployment framework confirms why no existing TXN shares should be sold to fund alternatives. Holding cash for TXN's $278.00–$286.00 support shelf (2.46:1 asymmetry) outranks swapping into shortlist peer Microsoft ($523.88, $660.00 target, 1.90:1 asymmetry) or outside peer NXP Semiconductors ($265.09, entry zone $242.42–$257.84, stop $234.07, $310.00 target, 1.65:1 asymmetry), keeping our 0.58% Schwab starter position intact.
